status: Source-fit design draft awaiting whole-claim/prerequisite and independent semantic review; no new associations authored, no coverage upgrade.
sourceIdentity: Accepted 2013 FSL identity; actual named Core Grade 4 digital hierarchy, not codename inference.
relationshipToPilot: Extends the seven-record pilot without changing its three adopted community claims or attribution. New draft designs address connected-message and strategy conditions left open there.
coverageBoundary: A complete authored task design is not evidence that a learner performed it. A general strategy posterior never certifies French competence; retain the actual language, variety, taught corpus, support and performance in the assessment record. No language or learner-state transfer is proposed.

materials: An adult-prepared, meaning-checked French corpus for familiar people, places, objects, actions and feelings; teach unfamiliar forms before assessment.
A qualified fluent model of the intended French variety, picture/realia supports, and a record of the exact utterances used.
checks: Check the meaning of spoken French by action, picture selection or a suitable response, separating understanding from French production.
Check independent appropriate retrieval after a few days and in a different familiar exchange. Immediate imitation or an English answer does not demonstrate French word production.
Preserve the three inherited French vocabulary/consonant/nasal-vowel claims completely, including their contrasting words, clusters, intended variety and transfer checks.
protocols.boundary: The declared taught corpus is a performance condition. This does not certify unrestricted French vocabulary or inherit proficiency from English.

materials: Three original, teacher-prepared oral French pieces with familiar taught language: a short classroom procedure, an account of an everyday event and an informative description. At least one literary read-aloud and one informational read-aloud exceed the learner's independent French reading ability.
A first unillustrated descriptive version and a separately supplied illustrated or performed version; the latter adds a relevant detail.
checks: Before each piece, state a listening purpose and activate relevant prior knowledge. During listening, choose and use more than one suitable strategy, then check the interpretation afterwards.
Recover connected facts and the purpose of each piece; answering one isolated vocabulary item does not establish message understanding. Ask and answer questions about actual details.
One detail is deliberately unclear in a non-deceptive way: the learner notices the gap and asks for a repeat or clarification rather than pretending to understand.
For the unillustrated passage, form or sketch a mental picture using heard details, explain an inference, then compare and revise it using the additional version.
Allow pointing, action, drawing or an appropriate first-language explanation to isolate listening; assess French production in its own tasks.
protocols.boundary: The strategy operations are shared. Every French expectation requires an actual French input attempt; a successful English task or a general-topic belief cannot certify French understanding.

materials: A familiar classroom scene, safe objects and a French sequence of four meaningful instructions using taught words; one instruction admits a genuine clarification question.
A second changed scene for the learner to direct a partner, with an agreed French ordering-word support.
checks: Follow all four spoken steps in order and ask about the unclear one; a visible full answer sequence must not replace listening.
Give clear, ordered spoken French directions to the partner, inspect the partner's result and identify a specific instruction to improve.
Change the objects or route for transfer. This tests connected meaning and interaction rather than recall of one four-step routine.
protocols.boundary: Four-step and partner-revision checks preserve the whole existing instructions claim; they are the designed component task, not an invented official French grade cutoff.

materials: Picture or object notes for familiar people and an everyday event, taught French expressions, optional auditory models for rehearsal and a recording/playback method.
A listener who does not already know the intended facts; a second familiar audience and topic.
checks: Prepare and give a brief coherent French description with several details. Speech is audible, ideas ordered and the intended meaning recoverable without an adult supplying every next sentence.

Include a one-minute report with at least three organised facts, and a separate personal-event recount with a beginning, middle and end. Review the recording for actual pace, clarity and relevant detail.
Use the supplied supports and rehearsal without substituting an adult-led list of isolated answers for the connected message.
Change audience and topic; select suitable learned French forms and enough detail for that listener.
protocols.boundary: The one-minute/three-fact checks preserve the existing report claim rather than redefine the source. Any broader whole-topic success is assessed separately from a narrower source component. No all-person conjugation claim is inferred from a memorised greeting.

materials: Two familiar audiences, a simple choice with different viewpoints and an agreed French corpus for expressing and responding to that choice.
A short statement/question exchange and a prepared presentation, with a qualified French pronunciation/intonation model.
checks: Choose a purpose and audience, use gestures or vocal choices to clarify the message, monitor whether the listener has understood and adjust one actual unclear detail.
In the choice discussion, listen to another view and respond with a relevant agreement, disagreement or extension and a reason; preserve the complete existing viewpoints claim.
Use different formality, tone or wording in a class presentation and a familiar conversation, explaining or showing the relevant choice. Formal-English production is not required or inferred.

In the actual French connected message and statement/question exchange, check smooth comfortable pace, phrasing, appropriate intonation and intelligibility of the taught words. A few correct isolated consonants or nasal vowels alone are insufficient.
Assess the intended variety's legitimate distinctions; no accent imitation, compulsory eye contact or a fixed non-verbal convention establishes success.
protocols.boundary: These are shared communication operations applied in French. The separate French language-performance record must remain attached to the actual attempt.

protocols.authorship: Original draft examples for this task, not official curriculum wording, recordings or observed learner responses. A qualified French model checks delivery and intended variety before actual use.

items.script: Prends un crayon bleu. Dessine un cercle au milieu de la feuille. Pose le crayon sous la feuille. Montre ton cercle à ton partenaire.
items.transfer: Change colour, shape or spatial relation after meanings are taught. A separate intentionally incomplete direction, Mets le petit objet ici, requires clarifying the location; teach a suitable request, then supply the missing information.

items.purpose: Understand and recount a familiar event
items.script: Samedi, Mina prépare son sac pour aller au parc avec son frère. Elle met une bouteille d’eau et un petit livre dans le sac. Au parc, il commence à pleuvoir. Mina et son frère rentrent à la maison. Ils regardent le livre ensemble.
items.checks: Identify who, intended destination, the change and its consequence. Order pictures only after listening; an already ordered picture sequence cannot supply the answer.

items.purpose: Infer from an unillustrated scene and revise with new evidence
items.script: Léo est devant la porte. Il tient son manteau et regarde les nuages gris. Son amie lui donne un parapluie.
items.checks: Form a picture from the heard details and suggest a supported feeling or next action, accepting more than one defensible inference. A separately supplied illustration shows Léo smiling; revise an earlier fear inference if the new evidence changes it. Do not claim that grey clouds guarantee rain.

items.purpose: Recover facts and message purpose from an oral description
items.script: Voici le chat de ma famille. Il a quatre pattes, deux oreilles et une longue queue. Il boit de l’eau et se repose sur son coussin. Quand il veut sortir, il attend près de la porte.
items.checks: Recover at least three supplied details and distinguish the described particular cat from a claim about every cat. Use taught vocabulary and a new description for transfer.

items.purpose: A different oral form and listening pattern
items.script: Dans mon sac, un petit livre. Dans ma main, un crayon bleu. Je m’assieds près de la porte. Et je dessine un oiseau.
items.checks: Recognise repeated structure and recover two details. This original verse is not claimed to rhyme; compare it with the narrative and instruction pieces by their purpose.

items.purpose: Connected production, audience and listener repair
items.modelOpening: Bonjour. Je vais vous parler de mon animal préféré. Voici trois choses à savoir…
items.checks: Use personal familiar facts to build a real one-minute report, not only this opening. Record and review it; then recount a different event and explain a game choice to a peer. Teach suitable French reason/response forms, such as Je préfère… parce que… and Je suis d’accord…, before eliciting them. Check the listener’s understanding and rephrase an unclear point.
items.boundary: The snippets are scaffolds, not evidence of a completed minute, three facts, varied audiences or independent message production.

rejectedRoutes.reason: The whole claim explicitly requires formal English. Its generic audience-adjustment component does not justify broadening or copying it into French.
The whole claim also includes quantitative and diverse-media summarising; not needed for this oral pilot.
The complete technical-vocabulary presentation claim adds independently broader evidence. Familiar-life message design can use existing describing/reporting claims.
Prior-knowledge activation is a useful task strategy, not a necessary extra taxonomy association. Its broad hard persistence gate is not needed to represent this source task.
Actual clarification/monitoring is explicit in the selected listening task. Adding a separate meta association and its help-seeking hard path is unnecessary for this slice.

next: Read complete hard-prerequisite closure and available guidance, prepare an original French resource packet, then request independent design review.
